<br>

I teach banking theory and evidence to Ph.D. students in the E. J. Ourso College of
Business, and I have taught corporate finance, financial institutions, and derivatives
across the undergraduate, MBA, and executive programs at LSU. I have delivered lectures
and conducted seminars for executives and technocrats in Brazil, China, the Czech
Republic, India, Malaysia, and South Africa.

My research focuses broadly on banking and financial markets, and has been published in
leading academic journals including the *Journal of Financial Economics*, the *Review of
Financial Studies*, and the *Journal of Money, Credit and Banking*. My interviews and
commentary have been featured in the *Wall Street Journal*, CNN/Money, Bloomberg, and
*Fortune*, as well as in regional outlets including the *Times-Picayune*, *The Advocate*,
the *Baton Rouge Business Report*, WBRZ-TV, and WWL-Radio.

I have mentored doctoral students, many of whom hold tenured faculty positions; organized
and led international consulting projects for MBA and MS students; and directed
undergraduate honors students who have won national thesis awards. Recently I have been
working on deposit stability, the information sensitivity of safe securities, appraisal
accuracy and loan collateral, and the financial economics of slavery.
